candidates.title: Honeybee: Locality-Enhanced Projector for Multimodal LLM
candidates.abstract: In Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), a visual projector plays a crucial role in bridging pre-trained vision encoders with LLMs, enabling profound visual understanding while harnessing the LLMs' robust capabilities. Despite the importance of the visual projector, it has been relatively less explored. In this study, we first identify two essential projector properties: (i) flexibility in managing the number of visual tokens, crucial for MLLMs' over-all efficiency, and (ii) preservation of local context from visual features, vital for spatial understanding. Based on these findings, we propose a novel projector design that is both flexible and locality-enhanced, effectively satisfying the two desirable properties. Additionally, we present comprehensive strategies to effectively utilize multiple and multifaceted instruction datasets. Through extensive experiments, we examine the impact of individual design choices. Finally, our proposed MLLM, Honeybee, remarkably outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods across various benchmarks, including MME, MMBench, SEED-Bench, and LLaVA-Bench, achieving significantly higher efficiency. Code and models are available at https://github.com/kakaobrain/honeybee.
candidates.reason: MLLMのvisual projectorで出力visual token数を柔軟に減らし、後段LLMの計算・memory・throughputを直接改善する設計。本文ではLLMがMLLM計算量の大半を占め、visual token数がresponse generation効率を左右すると明示し、C-Abstractor/D-Abstractorでlocalityを保ちながらtoken数を制御するためVLM推論効率の対象。
candidates.library_body_check: fulltext_relevance_review: arXiv一次PDFの§1、§3.1–3.2を確認。projectorがN visual featuresをM visual tokensへ変換し、Mを減らすことがLLM後段のcompute/memory/throughputを支配すること、C-AbstractorはResNet+adaptive average pooling、D-Abstractorはdeformable attentionでlocalityとtoken数柔軟性を両立することを確認。
